answer: An agent network can resist Sybil attacks by verifying optical physical unclonable functions. Each node authenticates by measuring light absorption through a randomized pigment film coated on a microfabricated ledge inside a secure vault. Because chaotic particle dispersion cannot be simulated, an attacker must fabricate discrete physical sensor modules per identity. However, photochemical decay over time alters the optical profile, requiring periodic recalibration.
